questions.text: In shadow, what exactly does the nightly comparison job do each night, and where do its results (the daily mismatch rate and counts) get written so gate A can read them?
questions.about: Gates and guards: shadow to both (gate A)

questions.text: When a person moves shadow to both, what actually changes at that moment? How do charging responsibility and ledger writing hand from the old engine to the new one for a billing period that is partly done?
questions.about: shadow --> both : person, gate A met

questions.text: Who or what measures the charge failure rate over a 10-minute window, and what does it count as a failure (declined cards, provider errors, timeouts)? What does the automatic trigger actually do to start the rollback?
questions.about: both --> RB_B : auto if charge failure rate over 2 pct in 10 min

questions.text: What is the 'ledger', and what is a 'billing period' here? Is the charge key one row per customer per period, and what is written when a charge is only 'unknown-outcome'?
In 'Resolve in-flight charges with payment provider', how is each unknown charge actually resolved, and who does it (a worker, or on-call)? What if the provider cannot say?
questions.about: B_drain / N_drain: Resolve in-flight charges with payment provider

questions.text: In both, the old engine computes into the shadow store but does not charge. In new_only the old engine stops computing. What are 'skipped usage events' and how does the old engine know which ones to reprocess in a new_only rollback?
questions.about: N_replay: Old engine reprocesses skipped usage events, no charging

questions.text: How do workers check the rollback record and the flag? Do they check before every charge, and what happens to a charge in progress at the moment the rollback record opens?
What does 'gates reset' mean concretely, and who records the Finance sign-off and the 'unresolved mismatch' list and marks mismatches resolved?

answers.text: Each night the job compares the two engines' invoices per customer (in shadow: old ledger vs new shadow store). It writes one result row per day (date, invoices compared, mismatches, rate) and updates the unresolved-mismatch list. Gate A reads those rows. Storage location is a design choice; I put it with the comparison job's results, not in the flag.

At the flip, the flag changes and the new engine takes over charging. Handover safety comes from the ledger rule: the engine taking over charges a period only if the ledger has no entry (including pending) for it. A half-done period is finished by whoever finds no entry, never charged twice. Whether to wait for a period boundary is not in the brief; recorded as open question 9.

The brief does not define a charge failure. I assumed provider errors and timeouts, not customer declines, and listed it in open question 4. A charge monitor counts new-engine charge attempts per 10-minute window and, above 2% failures, opens the rollback record, which halts new-engine charging; the rollback steps then run. Who owns the monitor is not decided.

The ledger is the billing ledger, the system of record. A billing period is the invoiced period for one customer. The key is one row per customer and period, with a uniqueness constraint. Before sending a charge the engine writes the row as pending; a pending row left after a crash or timeout is the unknown-outcome charge. It becomes charged or not charged when settled. Added to the file.

A rollback worker asks the payment provider about each pending charge by its idempotency key. Charged: complete the ledger entry. Not charged: mark it not charged so the old engine may charge it. If the provider cannot say, the rollback goes to RollbackBlocked and on-call decides. I chose the simplest handling and added no retry mechanism.

Skipped events are the usage events logged since new_only began, when the old engine stopped computing. The old engine replays from the new_only clock timestamp, which the file now says. In both, the old engine kept computing into the shadow store, so no replay is needed there.

Yes, a worker reads the flag and the rollback record before every charge. While a record is open, the new engine may not start a charge. A charge already sent when the record opens may finish or be left unknown; the drain step settles it via the ledger and provider. Added to the file.

Gates reset means all gate counters are cleared: consecutive-day count, compared-invoice count, days in both, and Finance sign-off, so the 7-day count starts over. The comparison job writes result rows and the mismatch list. A person marks mismatches resolved and records Finance sign-off. The tool for this is not decided; listed as open question 8.

questions.text: How does on-call actually start a manual rollback, and who or what runs the rollback steps afterwards: a worker automatically, or on-call by hand?
questions.about: Rollback entry points: both --> RB_B / new_only --> RB_N (on-call manual)

questions.text: In a rollback from both, between the halt and the flag flip, who charges? New engine is halted and old engine is not yet allowed. What happens to periods that fall due then?
questions.about: B_flag / N_flag: Set billing_mode to old_only

questions.text: Where does the replay write its recomputed invoices, and why must it finish before the flag flip? What does the old engine need that it lacks after new_only?
questions.about: N_replay: Old engine reprocesses skipped usage events, no charging

questions.text: For a period marked 'not charged' during the drain, how does the old engine learn it should charge it? Is that the same as 'no ledger entry', given a row exists?
How do the flag, the rollback record and the gate counters get cleared or closed when a rollback ends? Who closes the rollback record and when?
What does on-call actually do in RollbackBlocked for an unknown charge the provider can't confirm? How do they decide charged versus not charged?
questions.about: RollbackBlocked --> old_only : on-call finishes remaining steps, gates reset

questions.text: At the both to new_only flip, what stops the old engine's shadow-store computing, and how does the new_only clock get set?
questions.about: both --> new_only : person, gate B met and Finance sign-off

answers.text: On-call opens the rollback record (manual), or the charge monitor does (automatic). A rollback worker then runs all steps automatically in order. On-call acts only in RollbackBlocked. Added a 'Who runs it' paragraph. The exact tool for opening the record is not specified; that is a controller detail.

Nobody charges between the halt and the final catch-up. Periods falling due in that window wait and are charged in the catch-up step, so they are delayed, not dropped. I accept the delay because a double charge is worse. Stated explicitly in the file now.

The replay writes recomputed invoices to the shadow store, the same place the old engine wrote during both. It must finish before the flag flip because after new_only the old engine lacks invoices for the skipped window, and charging from an incomplete set would be wrong. The catch-up then charges from those invoices. The trade-off (flip first vs replay first) is open question 5. Added to the file.

Not the same as 'no entry' as written before, so I changed the handover rule: the taking-over engine charges a period if the ledger has no entry or the entry is marked not charged. Pending and charged entries are skipped. Fixed in the file and in the drain description.

The flag is set to old_only at the flag step. The rollback worker closes the rollback record after the last step; after RollbackBlocked, on-call closes it. Closing the record clears the gate counters. Added an 'Ending a rollback' paragraph replacing the old 'After any rollback' text.

Not known how on-call should decide charged vs not charged when the provider API cannot confirm. Plausible sources are the provider dashboard or the customer's bank records, but I have no verified procedure, and if still unclear the brief's two constraints (no double charge, no dropped charge) conflict. Added as open question 10 and pointed the drain text to it.

The person's move writes the flag and records the new_only clock together. The old engine stops computing when its workers next read the flag, since workers read it before work. A short lag where the old engine still computes into the shadow store is harmless. Added to the gate B row of the guards table.

questions.text: How long can a rollback step run before it counts as timed out, and what does 'nears 35 day expiry' mean in days or hours?
questions.about: RB_B --> RollbackBlocked : step fails or times out

questions.text: The diagram has no path from the shadow rollback to RollbackBlocked. If stopping the new engine or setting the flag fails there, what happens?
If the charge monitor or on-call tries to open a rollback record while one is already open, what happens? Also, if a rollback worker crashes in the middle of a step, who restarts it?
questions.about: Where state lives: Rollback progress (rollback record)

questions.text: What does decommissioning actually do to the flag, the old engine and the shadow store? Does anything still read billing_mode afterwards?

answers.text: The brief gives no step time limit, and I will not invent one. I removed 'times out' from the diagram and text, so a step fails only on an error or worker crash, and added open question 11 for the limit. 'Nears 35 day expiry' was vague, so I replaced it: the oldest skipped event is logged at the new_only clock, so it expires on day 35, and a replay not finished by then goes to RollbackBlocked.

You are right, the diagram lacked that edge. I added RB_S --> RollbackBlocked on step failure. All three rollbacks now share one failure rule: a failed step or crashed worker goes to RollbackBlocked and pages on-call, who finishes the remaining steps. I chose this as the simplest handling and added no retry.

Only one rollback record can be open at a time, and a second open request is ignored, because two workers running steps could double-act on the ledger. A crashed worker is treated as a failed step: the rollback goes to RollbackBlocked and on-call finishes from the step saved in the record. Nothing restarts automatically, which avoids a new takeover mechanism. Both are now in the 'Failures and restarts' paragraph.

Decommissioning is a person's decision after 35 days in new_only. The flag stays new_only, the old engine is removed, and no rollback exists afterwards, so no rollback logic reads the flag any more. Workers still read the flag as before. I added this to the gate table row. What happens to the shadow store and its retention is not decided; added as open question 12.

teachbacks.text:
1. Starting point. The rollout begins in `old_only`. The mode is the `billing_mode` flag in the config service, which is the only source of truth. Workers read it. In `old_only` the old engine computes invoices, charges, and writes the ledger. The new engine is off.

2. Enabling shadow. A person moves the rollout to `shadow`. There is no automated gate. The old engine still computes, charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger. New-engine errors here are only recorded. They never trigger a rollback, but they can raise the mismatch rate.

3. Nightly comparison. In `shadow` and `both`, a nightly job compares the two engines' invoices per customer. In `shadow` it compares the old engine's ledger invoices with the new engine's shadow-store invoices. A mismatch is a total that differs by more than 1 cent. The job writes one result row per night (date, invoices compared, mismatches, mismatch rate). It also updates the unresolved-mismatch list. These live with the job's results, not in the flag. If the job fails or doesn't run, that day doesn't count and the consecutive count is broken.

4. Gate A, `shadow` to `both`. A person makes the move once there have been 7 consecutive nights each under 0.1% mismatch. The document's assumption is that at least 5,000 invoices compared is the total across the window. The numeric gate can't be overridden. Charging passes from the old engine to the new one here, under the handover rule. The engine taking over charges a billing period only if the ledger has no entry for it, or the entry is `not charged`. Periods already charged or pending are skipped.

5. Running in `both`. The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice, but into the shadow store only, and doesn't charge. The nightly job now compares the new engine's ledger invoices with the old engine's shadow-store invoices. A mismatch becomes an unresolved mismatch. A person marks it resolved, and until then it blocks gate B.

6. Charging, which applies to the new engine in `both` or `new_only`. Before each charge, the worker reads the flag and the rollback record. If a rollback record is open, it must not start a charge, even if the flag still says `both` or `new_only`. Otherwise it writes a ledger row for the customer and billing period as `pending`. A uniqueness constraint allows one row per customer and period, so this reserves the period. It sends the charge to the payment provider with the same key as the idempotency key. The row then becomes `charged` or `not charged`. A `pending` row left after a crash counts as an unknown-outcome charge.

7. Gate B, `both` to `new_only`. A person moves it after at least 14 days in `both` with no unresolved mismatches, plus Finance sign-off. The move sets the flag and records the `new_only` clock together. Workers of the old engine stop computing when they next read the flag. The old engine therefore no longer produces invoices.

8. Running in `new_only`. The new engine is the one that computes, charges and writes the ledger. The `new_only` clock drives the day-35 cutoff.

9. Decommission. After 35 days in `new_only` with no rollback, a person may decommission. This is blocked while a rollback is in flight. The old engine is removed, the flag stays `new_only`, and nothing can be rolled back to afterwards.

10. Rollback triggers. On-call can start a manual rollback from `shadow`, `both` or `new_only`. In `new_only` it is refused from day 35. An automatic rollback is triggered by the charge monitor in `both` or `new_only` only. The monitor counts new-engine charge attempts per 10-minute window. It opens the record when the failure share is above 2%. Only one record can be open at a time. A second request while one is open is ignored. The rollback record sits beside the ledger. It holds the current step, the trigger, and the start time. Opening it stops new-engine charging at once, before the flag changes.

11. Rollback from `shadow`. The worker stops the new engine and sets the flag to `old_only`. No reconciliation is needed because the new engine never charged.

12. Rollback from `both`. The worker runs these steps in order, with no further input.
   - It halts new-engine charging.
   - It drains: for each in-flight or unknown-outcome charge, it asks the provider using the idempotency key. If the provider says it was charged, the worker completes the ledger entry. If not, it marks the entry `not charged`.
   - It sets the flag to `old_only`.
   - The old engine charges only periods with no live ledger entry. Its invoices are already current from the shadow store.

13. Rollback from `new_only`. The first two steps are the same: halt, then drain. After them:
   - The old engine reprocesses all usage events logged since the `new_only` clock. It writes the recomputed invoices to the shadow store, and it does not charge.
   - The flag is then set to `old_only`.
   - The old engine runs the catch-up. It charges periods with no live ledger entry, using the recomputed invoices.
   The usage log keeps events for 35 days, so replay must finish by day 35.

14. Between halt and catch-up nobody charges. Periods that fall due in that time wait and are charged in the catch-up.

15. Completing a rollback. The worker closes the record when the last step finishes. Closing it clears the gate counters: consecutive days, invoices compared, days in `both`, and Finance sign-off. The rollout restarts at `old_only` and must pass through `shadow` again. Earlier comparison results don't count.

16. Rollback failure. If any step fails, or the worker crashes, the rollback goes to `RollbackBlocked` and pages on-call. Nothing restarts automatically. The new engine stays halted. On-call finishes the remaining steps from the step saved in the record and closes the record. Gates reset and the rollout returns to `old_only`. The same blocked state follows if the provider cannot say whether a charge happened. In a `new_only` rollback it also follows when replay isn't done by day 35. That case is an urgent escalation.

17. Other failures. If the config service is unreachable, workers keep the last known mode. If they have none, they don't charge and they retry. The ledger uniqueness constraint backs this up if two engines briefly disagree on mode. If the automatic trigger fires after day 35 in `new_only`, no rollback is possible and it is treated as an incident on the new engine.
gaps: How on-call decides about a charge the provider cannot confirm, and what to do if it is still unclear. The document says this is undecided, so I cannot explain that step of RollbackBlocked.
How long a rollback step may run before it counts as failed. A hanging step is not detected, so I cannot say when RollbackBlocked is entered in that case.
What tool or mechanism people use to record Finance sign-off, resolve mismatches, and perform the manual mode moves and rollback requests. I cannot say how those inputs reach the gate counters.
Whether the shadow-to-both switch waits for a billing period boundary. The document assumes the ledger check is enough but says the brief does not settle it.
What counts as a charge failure for the 2% trigger (declines or only provider errors and timeouts). The document gives only an assumption. It also sets no minimum attempt count for low volume.
What happens to the shadow store and its retention after decommissioning. This is not decided.
